subject: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acmecorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-03-04T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request

Hi Olga / Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked us to confirm a couple of contract items before we move to legal: two points we need your help on are (1) an early-termination opt-out after an initial ramp period, and (2) an explicit ramp/downsell protection so we don't get hit with punitive pricing if our usage starts low and grows slower than forecast. High level:

- Early termination: we want a 60-day opt-out window that can be exercised at month 6 (i.e., customer may terminate after 6 months with 60 days' notice) with a modest termination fee rather than remaining committed months.
- Ramp schedule: propose a 12-month ramp with minimum billing floors for months 1–3 at 25% of committed capacity, months 4–6 at 50%, months 7–12 at 100%. We also want a downsell protection so that if we drop below the floor in months 7–12, pricing reverts to the then-current retail rate rather than a punitive uplift.

We understand these are non-standard; we can trade off by committing to a larger initial seat/usage forecast or longer contract term. Can you outline options and what flexibility is available on discounts and the opt-out? Procurement attached their checklist for reference.

Attachments: Acme_RFP_2026.pdf; Procurement-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Jordan Hayes
Head of AI Delivery
Acme Corp

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request

Team — looping you in for quick steer. Acme (large regional account) is asking for non-standard opt-out + downsell protections. They indicated willingness to increase forecast/term in exchange for the opt-out. My read: high value but downside risk if we give an unconstrained opt-out and heavy discounts.

Option A (Sales-favorable, requires exec signoff): Allow 60-day opt-out after month 6, with a termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed fee; accept the 12-month ramp floors (25/50/100) and cap aggregate discount at 25% for first 6 months. This gives the customer flexibility while retaining partial economic protection.

Option B (Conservative/legal-friendly): Require 90-day opt-out after month 9, termination fee equal to remaining committed months pro-rated, and tighten downsell protection so price reverts to list price with a 30% cure period. No discount >20% without exec approval.

Request: Marissa — can you confirm whether Option A is workable from legal/finance (I suspect we need to tighten the termination fee language). Vivek — need your ok for any discount >20% and acceptance of Option A's termination fee approach. Priyom — I’ll draft a short term sheet to send to Acme once we have alignment.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Director | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachment: Proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request

Olga / Priyom — reviewed. High-level comments:

- We can accept a 60-day opt-out but only after a longer initial commitment window (recommend month 9) or with a meaningful termination fee. The fee should be defined (e.g., 50% of remaining committed payments or a fixed sum equal to 3 months' average billing), not an ambiguous "modest" fee.
- Ramp floors (25/50/100) are fine as a commercial construct, but we should add a clear remediation path: if usage falls below the floor in months 7–12, customer has a 30-day cure period; failure to cure results in reversion to list pricing for the shortfall months and a reconciliation invoice. This limits revenue leakage.
- Discounts: any upfront discount >20% requires VP approval (Vivek). For pricing math we should include an example line item in the SOW so finance can model ARR impact.

Suggested redline changes (summary):
1) Change opt-out trigger to "after month 9" OR accept "after month 6" only if termination fee = 50% of remaining committed fees and the customer pays a one-time transition assistance fee equal to one month of committed billing.
2) Define "downsells" and associated cure/repricing mechanics.
3) Insert a clawback for promotional credits if the contract terminates early.

If you want I can prepare a redline to send to Acme; Priyom, please confirm whether we are willing to anchor the discount to 25% for first six months as a negotiating start.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-05T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request

Thanks for the summary. I authorize moving forward with a customer-friendly posture but with guardrails. Approve Option A with the following conditions:

- Opt-out allowed no sooner than month 6 but only if we secure a minimum revenue guarantee (MRG) equal to 50% of committed billing for the remaining term OR a termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed fees (choose one).
- Discounts: cap any total discount at 25% for the first six months; any program-level discount beyond 20% requires my explicit written approval.
- Ramp/downsell: accept the 12-month ramp (25/50/100) but require a 30-day cure period and automatic true-up to list price for under-usage during months 7–12. Also add a clause that promotional credits are forfeited on termination.

Olga — please send the redline to Acme with those bullets and include a short cover note offering a single-call negotiation to finalize. Priyom/Marissa — loop me if Acme pushes materially on the termination fee or discount cap.

-Vivek
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract: Early termination & ramp language — request

Jordan — thanks for outlining Acme's needs. We appreciate the flexibility and have reviewed internally. We can accommodate the requested ramp structure with the safety rails below (summary of what we've redlined):

- Ramp: 12-month ramp with minimum billing floors of 25% (months 1–3), 50% (months 4–6), 100% (months 7–12).
- Opt-out: Customer may elect early termination beginning at month 6 with 60 days' notice only if either (a) a minimum revenue guarantee (MRG) of 50% of remaining committed fees is paid at termination, or (b) a termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed fees is paid.
- Downsells/Under-usage: 30-day cure period; failure to cure triggers automatic true-up to list pricing for the shortfall and a reconciliation invoice. Promotional credits are forfeited upon termination.
- Discount: We are prepared to offer a commercial discount capped at 25% for the first six months. Any discount above 20% required written approval from Redwood leadership (we have already obtained conditional approval up to 25%).

I've attached the redline for your review (Redline_Acme_Ramp_20260306.pdf) and included a DocuSign link to the updated agreement if you are comfortable with the changes: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?d=0a1b2c3d4e5f

If you'd like, let's do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the redline and confirm the termination/fee mechanics so legal can finish procurement sign-off. Please let me know preferred times.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Director | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0129
